title: Live chain at 12 km: +26 m cross-range and +50 m range bias (popoto_vehicle chain)
description: Measured after D-156 on popoto_12km seeds 51-60, host backend, configs/deploy/popoto_vehicle.yaml chain: Python, C++ and sonar_live agree to 5e-6 m. Report error at last ping: range +49.5 m (unchanged by D-156), cross-range +26.1 m mean (was -23.1 m before D-156, the old -48 m timing error was partly cancelling it). Speed 6.1 vs 6.0 m/s. Hypothesis (unchecked): detections placed from the array pose at transmit (array_frame(record)); ownship moves ~24 m during the 16 s round trip. Range +50 m cause unknown. Outputs: scratchpad/measure/live12_after, a12_after.json.
notes:
Diagnosis (scratchpad/diag2hz): (1) cross-range +26 m = +49 m fit lag (report fits a line through Kalman-filtered history; tracks born at zero velocity with bearing_sigma 1 deg = 210 m at 12 km vs real 0.03-0.05 deg; noise-free +38.7 m) partly cancelled by (2) -46 m coherent glint of the 5-point ship at the abeam last ping (single point: -1.5 m). (3) range +49.5 m = energy-weighted centroid of a multipath-spread echo (extent ~120 m); leading edge -0.8 m. Ownship motion during round trip is compensated by backprojection rx velocity (control: -24 m without it). Scoring correct. Proposed: fit measured positions; opt-in leading-edge range; glint is target model/scoring.
D-157 merged (c9300f9): measured-position fit (A, default), cfar.range_estimate first (B, opt-in), outline scoring (C); review fixes 04893f5, ddaa417. Live 12 km A+B: range +0.9 m, cross-range -23.3 m (glint), hull distance 1.0 m. Follow-ups filed.
close_reason: D-157 merged and both suites pass (CPU 157/157 on 605a4e1, GPU job 6b0249a54fdc5ab3c55f0b8f 1679 passed). Remaining glint error in sonar-ljh; default range estimate in sonar-1p2.

title: popoto_12km ship misclassified: a mover on only 3 of 10 seeds (uncertain/multipath, speed about half)
description: Merged from sonar-ic5 (12 km part) and sonar-ofa. Committed gallery (job 6b013d75efaf5e14f4b47980): ship tracked 24 m off, track velocity (-3.17, 0.01) m/s vs true (-6, 0), kind uncertain; scene counts mover 4, multipath 4, uncertain 4, no false movers. History: mover, then uncertain after the detector rework (4530dc4: 4.3 +/- 1.0 m/s), multipath on ebdb22a, uncertain 3.3 m/s since. tools/classify_rules_eval.py over 10 seeds: correct on 3 of 10; the detection rules do not change it. Cause not investigated.
notes:
Diagnosis 2026-11-21 from the 10 seed captures of tools/classify_rules_eval.py (job 6b0130d0efaf5e14f4b46b34), no new simulation. (1) The ship gives 11-13 confirmed tracks on every seed, all within 170 m of it, at ranges from the true range (11,853 m) to about 130 m beyond: its arrivals by longer paths in 100 m of water. Nearly every one has about the ship's velocity (5-7 m/s west). (2) The gallery scores the ship by the NEAREST track to the truth; with a dozen copies that is a coin toss among them (often a short 4-point track born at ping 3, which cannot be a mover from 4 points, or a multipath child): the 3-of-10 and the '3.3 m/s' (k0 id 9, 4 points, rms 21 m) come from this. Reproduced: nearest track mover on k4, k5, k7 exactly. (3) Echo grouping takes the STRONGEST track as the object and only groups weaker tracks FARTHER out in range. The strongest arrival is 50-83 m beyond the true range on every seed (a later path, not the direct one); the earliest arrival (within 3 m of the true range on 9 of 10 seeds) is weaker, so it and other early arrivals are never grouped: 3-6 tracks stay mover/uncertain per seed. (4) Only 6 pings (20 s apart), so tracks born after ping 2 have 4 points and stay uncertain by the Student-t rule. Not a tracker velocity bug. Fix options for the owner: scoring by object (any non-multipath track within the gate, or the group), grouping that takes the earliest arrival as the object or groups both sides in range, more pings in the scenario.

Fixed by D-155 (merged): echo grouping transitive on both sides, object = earliest established arrival; gallery scores the object. Re-score of 120 captures: ship one mover on 10/10 seeds. Gallery regeneration on GPU pending at the time of this note.
close_reason: D-155 merged; regenerated gallery (job 6b01577eefaf5e14f4b49804): ship one mover at 6.05 m/s, 68 m off; 10/10 seeds in the re-score. Follow-ups: cross-range error, chain-merge risk, elevation demotion (filed).

title: HSB receiver stalls ~75-110 ms after each ping (loopback socket-buffer margin)
description: D-160 study (HF jobs 6b03468b8d268c0fbd228881, 6b03468c130a00b5aa80fa64): every lost frame falls 12-18 frames after a ping completes, with either range estimate; halved buffer loses alike; reserving the receiver core does not help. Normal 212,992 B buffer loses 1 frame in a few % of runs. Find what stalls the receiving process during ping processing (e.g. GIL held by chain stages), fix, and make the loopback test robust.
notes:
Investigation (inv-stall eecb5e4, 6 HF jobs): receiver waits 5-13 ms runnable (run-queue wait) during OpenMP backprojection_map (8 threads on 8 SMT vCPUs); not GIL (probe), not steal (0). Half buffer loss 9/15; with chain OpenMP 4 threads 0/10 (normal 0/6), worst latency 10-13 -> 1-2 ms, +10% chain time. Isolating/pinning receiver, nice 10, 7 threads, C++ engine: still lose. HSB 2.7.0 receiver thread is unpinned by default (inv-hsb reserve_core test was invalid). Proposed: opt-in receive --chain-omp-threads, loopback test at cpu_count//2 plus worst receive latency < 5 ms assertion. Awaiting owner.
Owner decision 2026-11-22: opt-in receive --chain-omp-threads; loopback test uses cpu_count//2 and asserts worst receive delay < 5 ms (no retries, buffer unchanged); DEPLOYMENT advice; other defaults unchanged.
close_reason: Merged (D-162); loopback 8/8, GPU suite 1809 passed
